description:
Open-source, multiplatform program for playing tabletop card games over a network


Available pre-compiled binaries for installation:
  Windows
   • Windows 10+
  macOS
   • macOS 15+ Sequoia
   • macOS 14+ Sonoma
   • macOS 13+ Ventura (x86)
  Linux
   • Ubuntu 26.04 LTS Resolute Racoon
   • Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Noble Numbat
   • Debian 13 Trixie
   • Debian 12 Bookworm
   • Fedora 44
   • Fedora 43
   General Linux support is available via a flatpak package hosted at Flathub (x86 & ARM)!
   Thanks to courtesy of @FFY00, the app is also available in Arch Linux's official extra repository.
 We maintain a Docker image for "Servatrice" in GHCR (x86 & ARM). You can docker pull it or use our Docker Compose files!
General Notes
We're pleased to announce the newest official release: Cockatrice 3.1.2: Reality Check
Note
Cockatrice 3.1.2 is our follow-up fix release for all the bugs and regressions that the feature release 3.1.0 introduced.
For a full list of new features, see the 3.1.0 release log!
Feature releases are always accompanied by follow-up fix releases to incorporate any community feedback. We depend on you to improve and surface hidden bugs. Read on to learn about how to help us! We're also urgently looking for more developers! Reach out to us in the #dev chat on Discord!
We hope you enjoy the changes made! All improvements with their corresponding tickets since the last version of Cockatrice are listed in the changelog below.
Note
This version of Cockatrice introduces automated crash reporting using Sentry. Should Cockatrice crash, you'll be given the option to send a helpful debug log to the developers. These really help us in fixing those crashes and ensuring they don't happen again. We hope you'll participate in making Cockatrice better :)
If you ever encounter a bug, have a suggestion or idea, or feel a need for a developer to look into something, please feel free to open a ticket. (How to create a Ticket for Cockatrice)
For basic information related to the app and getting started, please take a look at our official site: https://cockatrice.github.io
If you'd like to help and contribute to Cockatrice in any way, check out our README.
We're always available to answer questions you may have on how the program works and how you can provide a meaningful contribution.

Upgrading Cockatrice
Important
This release changes the way passwords are stored on your device and generated.
For most users: you don't have to do anything but enjoy the heightened security and the fact that your password is no longer stored on disk in plaintext.
Users who wish to continue using older clients: When you log in with a new client, your password is converted to the new Scrypt format and your old MD5 password is "sealed" inside the database with an encryption key. You have 180 days from the time it is sealed to use it to login again (i.e. login with an old client) after which it is expunged. Logging in with an old client during these 180 days refreshes them.
Run the internal software updater: Help → Check for Client Updates
Don't forget to update your card database right after! (Help → Check for Card Updates...)
